payload.blocks: The admission rule of the split between ready (quality) and queued (delivery), §3 row 2. Rows 7, 12, 13 and the referee work go on without it.
payload.headline: A ready plan that is not in the delivery queue: does it still start by itself?

parts.cause: Today one status carries both meanings: the supervisor starts any ready plan once its blockedBy are done and a lead slot is free (supervision spec l.131; portfolio.rs admissible()). Your own release sequence holds draft plans, so queue membership must be a separate field, not a status value.

options.cost: Admission rule change plus the queue field; the secretary queues plans on your orders.
options.does: Admission = ready AND queued AND referee accepts AND a lead slot is free. A ready plan outside the queue waits.
options.gain: Validation never starts delivery by accident; the queue is the only delivery order, held on trunk.
options.harm: Every plan must be queued by someone, or it sits ready forever.
options.label: Only queued plans are delivered

options.cost: Same queue field; admission gets two tiers.
options.does: Queued plans go first in queue order; when the queue has nothing admissible, other ready plans start by priority as today.
options.gain: No plan sits idle; today's flow keeps working for unqueued plans.
options.harm: Ready still partly means deliver now; an unqueued plan can take a lead slot you meant for the next step.
options.label: Queued first, then any ready plan

parts.recommendation: Only queued plans are delivered: it is the clean form of the split you asked for, and the secretary already writes your orders into the portfolio.

scope.allows: Records the admission rule in the discussion; the planner writes it into the supervision spec, plan contract and admission code.
scope.forbids: Does not choose the queue field's name or who writes it (row 7); does not change the plans already running.

parts.what: You asked to separate ready (the plan is complete and validated, fit to do) from queued (the plan is in the delivery queue). Splitting them leaves one choice: what the supervisor does with a ready plan nobody has queued.
